children.translated_text: for liberation from the bonds of worldly existence,
the key that opens the door of discrimination.
This is the stairway to liberation,
this is the deception of death;
that by which the mind, turned away from delusion,
becomes attached to the supreme Self.
Of the <s>śruti</s>-wish-fulfilling tree whose branches are frequented by the twice-born,
which alleviates the torment of worldly existence—
as there are species of living beings;
one is declared to be <s>siddhāsana</s> (the accomplished posture),
Having firmly placed the heel at the <s>yoni-sthāna</s> (perineum), one should steadily place

children.text: meḍhre pādam athaikam eva niyataṃ kṛtvā samaṃ vigraham
children.translated_text: one foot upon the phallus, keeping the body straight and steady;
motionless, with senses restrained and gaze unwavering, looking at the space between the eyebrows—
this, which opens the door to liberation, is called <s>siddhāsana</s> (the accomplished posture).

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ hi caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot upon the left thigh, and likewise the left

children.text: dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: upon the right thigh, firmly grasping [the toes] from behind with both hands,

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayed
children.translated_text: pressing the chin to the chest and fixing the thumbs [at the heart], one should gaze at the tip of the nose—
this, which destroys diseases and ailments, is called <s>padmāsana</s> (the lotus posture) for <s>yamins</s> (the self-controlled).
between the two is the <s>yoni-sthāna</s> (seat of creation),
which is called <s>kāma-rūpa</s> (the form of desire).
In the place called <s>ādhāra</s>, at the region of the anus,
in the middle of that is proclaimed the <s>yoni</s> (source),
In the middle of the <s>yoni</s> is a great <s>liṅga</s>,
one who knows it as split like a jewel at its head
flashing like a streak of lightning,
this is designated as being below the phallus.
By the word 'sva' is meant <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath);
the region of the phallus is designated.
Where the <s>kanda</s> (bulb) is strung like a jewel on a thread
Above the phallus and below the navel,
the <s>kanda-yoni</s> (root-bulb) is shaped like a bird's egg;
ten are further mentioned as important.
and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> is mentioned as the tenth;
<s>Iḍā</s> is situated on the left side,
<s>Kuhū</s> in the region of the genitals,
these three <s>nāḍīs</s> are enumerated [as the chief ones].
those beginning with <s>Nāga</s> are the five well-known [subsidiary airs],
and those beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s> are the five <s>vāyus</s> (winds);
these dwell within the thousands of <s>nāḍīs</s>
in the form of the living being.
The <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), under the control of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>,
along the left and right pathways,
due to its restlessness, it is not seen.
Just as a ball struck on the ground
Just as a hawk bound by a rope,
even when it flies away, is pulled back,
so the <s>jīva</s>, bound by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature),
these two are situated above and below—
one who knows this is a knower of <s>yoga</s>.
the opening of the gate of <s>Brahman</s>
she always covers with her mouth.
and struck by the mind and the wind,
taking up the quality of the living being,

children.text: vakṣo-nyasta-hanur nipīḍya suciraṃ yoniṃ ca vāmāṅghriṇā
children.translated_text: Pressing the chin firmly to the chest, pressing the <s>yoni</s> (perineum) for a long time with the left foot,

children.text: hastābhyām avadhāritaṃ prasaritaṃ pādaṃ tathā dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: holding the outstretched right foot firmly with both hands,

children.text: āpūrya śvasanena kukṣi-yugalaṃ baddhvā śanai recayed
children.translated_text: filling the cavity of the abdomen with breath, then slowly exhaling—

children.text: eṣā pātaka-nāśinī sumahatī mudrā nṝṇāṃ procyate
children.translated_text: this great <s>mudrā</s>, which destroys sins, is proclaimed for people.
The tongue, inserted into the cavity of the palate,
turned upward in the reverse direction,
with the gaze directed between the eyebrows—
this is the <s>mudrā</s> called <s>khecarī</s> (moving in space).
Above the phallus and below the navel—
the mastery of <s>uḍḍiyāna bandha</s> (the flying-up lock)
is a lion against the elephant of death.
When the <s>jālandhara bandha</s> (net-holder lock) is performed,
characterized by the contraction of the throat,
the nectar does not fall into the [digestive] fire,
nor does the breath become agitated.
Since even <s>Brahmā</s>, out of fear of death,
therefore one should restrain the breath.
When the breath moves, everything moves;
when it is still, everything becomes still;
therefore one should restrain the breath.
through the left and right pathways—
with gaze fixed on the tip of the nose, alone,
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the breath dwelling in the body;
by that the <s>yogin</s> reaches the sky.
should fill [the breath] through the <s>candra</s> (moon, left nostril);
having retained it as long as possible,
one should then exhale through the <s>sūrya</s> (sun, right nostril).
white and radiant like the ocean of milk,
Drawing the breath through the <s>sūrya</s> (sun, right nostril),
one should fill the abdomen slowly;
having retained it according to the prescribed method,
one should then exhale through the <s>candra</s> (moon, left nostril).
meditating on it as situated at the navel, the <s>yogin</s>
and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention), which is of the nature of <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>)—
In the inferior [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] there are twelve <s>mātrās</s>,
in the middle, twice that number,
in the superior, three times the <s>mātrās</s>—
In the inferior, there is profuse perspiration;
in the superior, the <s>yogin</s> rises up
with the perspiration produced by exertion;
one should maintain a diet of milk.
One should inhale the breath gently, gently,
one should not retain the breath excessively,
being led to the crown of the head by the <s>śakti</s> (power),
one is freed from all sins.
the destroyer of the fuel of sin,
the great bridge across the ocean of transgressions—
so it is always proclaimed by the <s>yogins</s>.
One woman is enjoyed by two—
she who has come from the lunar sphere;
the third one who unites with those two—
In the region of the navel dwells one—
the sun, of the nature of fire;
of the nature of nectar, ever situated
at the root of the palate, is the moon.
one should know the technique by which
The navel is above, the palate below;
the sun is above, the moon below—
is obtained from the mouth of the guru.
Where the bull, bound in three ways,
the <s>yogins</s> know to be at the heart.
having attained the great lotus of <s>prāṇa</s>—
By the syllable 'vi' is remembered <s>haṃsa</s> (the swan/breath);
therefore, at the throat, the one called <s>viśuddha</s> (specially pure)—
having held the water of the lunar digit (<s>soma-kalā</s>),
within a month it does not diminish,
having deceived the mouth of the sun.
Pressing with the tip of the tongue
the great cavity of the royal tooth,
meditating on the goddess made of nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) —
within six months one becomes a poet (<s>kavi</s>).
For the yogin whose body is filled with nectar,
the arising of qualities such as <s>aṇimā</s> [atomic minuteness] and others [occurs].
Just as fire [does not leave] its fuel,
and a lamp [does not leave] its oil-wick,
so the embodied one whose [body] is filled with the lunar digit
In the heart, the <s>dhāraṇā</s> of the five elements
through the steadiness of the mind,
The earth [element], beautiful as the region of yellow orpiment, yellow, associated with the syllable 'la',

children.text: saṃyuktā kamalāsanena hi catuṣkoṇā hṛdi sthāyinī
children.translated_text: conjoined with the lotus-seated [<s>Brahmā</s>], four-cornered, abiding in the heart —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.

children.text: eṣā stambhakarī sadā kṣitijayaṃ kuryād bhuvo dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the earth <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which causes immobility and always brings mastery over the earth.
Resembling a half-moon, white as <s>kunda</s> flowers, the water element stationed in the throat,
endowed with the seed-syllable 'va' of nectar, always conjoined with <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.
This is the water <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which should be the remedy for the unbearable poison of <s>Kāla</s> [Death].
The element stationed at the palate, resembling an <s>indragopa</s> [firefly], brilliant and triangular,
consisting of fire and the syllable 'ra', beautiful as coral, conjoined with <s>Rudra</s> —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.

children.text: eṣā vahni-jayaṃ sadā vidadhate vaiśvānarī dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the <s>vaiśvānara</s> [fire] <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which always brings mastery over fire.

children.text: yad bhinnāñjana-puñja-sānnibham idaṃ tattvaṃ bhruvor antare
children.translated_text: That element between the eyebrows, resembling a mass of crushed collyrium,
circular, consisting of air, associated with the syllable 'ya', where <s>Īśvara</s> is the deity —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.

children.text: eṣā khe gamanaṃ karoti yamināṃ syād vāyavī dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the air <s>dhāraṇā</s> of the disciplined, which causes movement through the sky.
The space [element], resembling perfectly pure water, stationed in the <s>brahmarandhra</s> [crown aperture],
therein, always conjoined with <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the peaceful syllable 'ha' —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing the <s>prāṇa</s> there, one should hold [it] for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> with the mind focused.
This is the space <s>dhāraṇā</s>, declared to be skilled in breaking open the door of liberation.
are the five <s>dhāraṇās</s> of the elements.
By action, by mind, and by speech,
the five <s>dhāraṇās</s> are difficult to attain.
The yogin who practices them constantly
When the mind is established in the ultimate reality (<s>tattva</s>),
<s>Saguṇa</s> is through the distinction of colors [forms];
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one is freed from sin.
beautifully adorned like a fine ruby —
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one is freed from transgression.
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one agitates the world.
Like lightning's radiance in the heart-lotus,
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one becomes filled with <s>Brahman</s>.
Constantly, in the middle of the bell [throat center],
the pure one, from which nectar arises —
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one becomes filled with <s>Brahman</s>.
The deity situated between the eyebrows,
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one becomes filled with bliss (<s>ānanda</s>).
in the sky, facing all directions —
fixing the gaze at the tip of the nose
and meditating, one is freed from suffering.
The anus, the genitals, the navel,
between the eyebrows — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>),
pure, of the nature of space,
meditating on the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) as all-pervading,
[those] endowed with the reality of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>)
produce the arising of the eight powers (<s>guṇa</s>).
differently according to the color [placed near it].
When freed from the distinctions of power (<s>śakti</s>),
knowers of reality (<s>tattva</s>) know the reality.
The five sense-objects beginning with sound,
as long as they are perceived in the ears and other [senses],
only that long is meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) remembered;
then the oneness of equal essence (<s>samarasa</s>)
Neither smell, nor taste, nor form,
the yogin knows neither self nor other,
As milk [is hidden] in milk, ghee in ghee,
the knower of yoga, in the supreme state.
Fire in the forest of the fear of worldly existence,
the knower of yoga, in the supreme state.
